about: 史实与创作对照的同步记号。Script_HistoryLedgerAudit.mjs 读它决定从哪里开始看改动、--check 读它拦已否决的链接；skill tengxian-fact-fiction-sync 核对完用 --mark-reviewed 写回。

assetReviews.scope: Independent reference-led candidate only; no replacement of the current whitebox bridge or story. Preserve global reviewedAt/repoCommit and unrelated page/source cursors.
assetReviews.decision: Exact A remains 0: no confirmed photograph of the 1938 Beishahe bridge was found. Low half-through truss form is a creative comparison with JACAR neighboring bridges and a 1934 Xianning bridge, not an exact historical reconstruction. Span count, dimensions, piers, paint, wear and concealed hardware remain inferred.
assetReviews.sourceReview: Official PDF request returned 200/application/pdf; original complete scan pages and photo 6/12 crops were opened. Photo 12 is captioned Tengxian north 1 km / 567 km; photo 6 is 560 km Jiehe. Neither is identified as the Beishahe bridge. Metadata page returned 403 to the web reader; it was not treated as verified page text.
assetReviews.scaleBoundary: Modern OSM railway bridge segments and Esri imagery constrain a present-day floodplain crossing of about 280 m; the visible main channel is about 35-50 m. These are modern map estimates, not evidence of bridge length, pier positions or water level in March 1938. The candidate 14 x 20 m short spans and 1.435 m gauge are design choices, not Beishahe-specific archival measurements.
assetReviews.generatedReferenceBoundary: Imagegen studies supplement local construction detail and material design only; generated images are not historical photographs or evidence.
assetReviews.detailBoundary20261027: Paired rivet rows, steel/wood/stone surface textures, individual masonry color variations and scattered lower-pier water or mud staining are reconstruction choices. They do not establish the original 1938 bridge surface, its waterline or local hydrological condition. The American 1908 road bridge is only a distant construction comparison, not evidence about Tengxian.
assetReviews.deckBoundary20261028: The independent candidate's transverse solid timber deck, its layout and texture are reference-based design choices; no available photograph establishes the 1938 Beishahe bridge deck. The existing whitebox's sleeper-only deck description remains its own separate setting.

trussReview20261030.decision: The candidate's central crossed braces and end-bay diagonals are a visual analogy to the modern Xianning bridge photograph in the user's research page. That photograph's date and original photographer remain unverified, and it does not identify the 1938 Beishahe bridge's members. No bridge-specific historical claim is added.
trussReview20261030.scope: Only the existing bridge creative row, parent bullet and player-facing creative entry were updated. Preserve global review anchors and unrelated page cursors.

steelFinishReview20261030.decision: A separate brown-gray truss finish is generated from the modern Xianning comparison image. The source image's date and original photographer remain unverified; neither its rust nor the generated material establishes the 1938 Beishahe bridge's paint or condition. The rail keeps a separate neutral steel texture.
steelFinishReview20261030.notionReview: The existing bridge creative row and parent bullet were reread. Their explicit creative boundaries for color, weathering and steel textures already cover this material-only iteration; no category or historical claim changes. Global review anchors and unrelated page cursors remain unchanged.

pierWeatherReview20261030.decision: The candidate's mottled lower-pier staining and weathered-stone texture are authored from an AI construction study and an additional generated texture. They do not establish the 1938 waterline, vegetation, or original masonry condition.
pierWeatherReview20261030.notionReview: The existing bridge creative row and parent bullet were reread; both already identify lower-pier water and mud marks and steel/wood/stone textures as design inferences. No historical claim or category changes. Global review anchors and unrelated page cursors remain unchanged.

nodeConnectionReview20261030.decision: Extended upper gussets, packers and rivet heads are an authored engineering analogy to HAER WV-64 photo 14 of the Easley road bridge, built in 1936. Wikimedia Commons dates the photograph to 1997. This is neither a railway-bridge photograph nor evidence for Beishahe's original nodes, dimensions or fasteners.
nodeConnectionReview20261030.sourceReview: The LOC record was available in indexed text but its original page returned HTTP 403 during this check. The image and attribution were examined via the Wikimedia Commons public-domain file page; no location or date was transferred to Beishahe.
nodeConnectionReview20261030.notionReview: The existing creative bridge row and parent bullet were reread; their explicit boundaries for unseen details and rivets already cover this node-only iteration. No historical claim or category changes. Global review anchors and unrelated page cursors remain unchanged.

deckFixingReview20261030.decision: Paired fasteners on the authored transverse wood deck are a visual analogy to general timber-bridge plank connections, not documented 1938 Beishahe fasteners. Their 71 mm simplified cylinders and 25 mm bearer embed are design choices, not an engineering-compliance claim.
deckFixingReview20261030.sourceReview: The 2005 FHWA covered-bridge manual was opened: it discusses deck planks spiked to supporting stringers or floor beams and commonly two spikes per connection. It is an American highway-bridge analogy; its vehicular-deck minimum dimensions are not claimed for this model.
deckFixingReview20261030.notionReview: The existing creative bridge row and parent bullet were reread. Both state that the transverse deck and unseen details are design inferences, so no historical claim or category changes. Global review anchors and unrelated page cursors remain unchanged.

pierJointReview20261030.decision: Depth-related darkening across the existing stone bevels is an authored occlusion-style treatment guided by the AI construction study. It does not establish mortar color, masonry appearance, or lighting on the 1938 Beishahe bridge.
pierJointReview20261030.notionReview: The existing bridge creative row and parent bullet were reread; their boundaries for stone textures, appearance, and unseen bridge details already cover this visual-only iteration. No historical claim or category changes. Global review anchors and unrelated page cursors remain unchanged.

pierMasonryReview20261030.decision: Variable stone lengths, staggered course joints and corner seam positions are authored visual analogies to the AI construction study. They do not establish the original Beishahe masonry bond or block dimensions. A newly generated stone texture was compared and not adopted.
pierMasonryReview20261030.notionReview: The existing bridge creative row and parent bullet were reread. Their explicit boundaries for piers, stone textures, dimensions and unseen details cover this iteration; no historical claim or category changes. Global review anchors and unrelated page cursors remain unchanged.

pierEdgesReview20261030.decision: Unequal stone-corner bevels and their visual occlusion transition are authored analogies to the rough masonry in the AI construction study, not measured damage or dimensions of the 1938 bridge.
pierEdgesReview20261030.notionReview: The bridge creative row and parent bullet were reread. Their explicit boundaries for pier dimensions, stone appearance, wear and unseen details cover this edge treatment; no historical claim or category changes. Global review anchors and unrelated page cursors remain unchanged.

assetReviews.scope: Signal and white parachute illumination effects only. Preserve global audit cursors and unrelated history reviews.
assetReviews.decision: TM-E 30-480 (1944) chapter X section 17 was opened and verified: colored stars, parachute variants and reported 4–15 s signal-pistol burning time. It does not identify the 1938 Tengxian shot. Exact staging, color meaning, canopy appearance, luminance and trajectories remain reconstruction choices.
assetReviews.structureReview: Verified title page: Ministry of Home Security, 3rd edition, 1944; section 15 and figure 57. German aerial flare structure and burnt-out remains are period comparisons, not measurements of the Japanese small flare. AWM REL31335 is dated circa 1953 and is used only as a fabric/attachment material study. No Tengxian use claim upgraded.
assetReviews.acceptanceScope: Historical optical distinction, shared game/editor lifecycle, actual rendered-roof contact, spatial audio, packed depth shadows and bounded night metering verified. See Data_FlareRealismAudit for exact tests, existing unrelated EditorTest failures and reconstruction limits. Global audit cursors unchanged.
assetReviews.illuminationReview: Original title and printed pp.70–71 verified: Military Intelligence Division, War Department, 20 July 1945; Type95 (1935), 70mm parachute illumination, approx.20s / 90,000 candlepower. Explicitly not recovered; Japanese-source intelligence, not specimen measurement or Tengxian use proof. Height, descent, wind, canopy and scene exposure remain reconstruction.

assetReviews.scope: Only the independent cloth-lab quilt, door curtain, Sichuan banner and generic material comparison samples; preserve global repoCommit, reviewedAt and unrelated source-page stamps
assetReviews.decision: Quilt loft, quilting, wear, curtain appearance and all simulation choices are artistic study. The banner uses a Sichuan death-flag motif; red diagonal bands, borders, typography, proportions and deformation are artistic choices, not an exact original reproduction or a Tengxian presence claim.
assetReviews.appearanceReview: DongguaQuilt V4 only: faded grey-blue cotton face, warm-grey cotton lining, uneven soft filling and rounded binding replace the former large patches and leather-like surface detail. Colour, weave, wear, quilting and edge construction remain artistic material-study choices, not a documented 1938 issue pattern or an original-object reproduction. DoorCurtain, SichuanBanner and the production blanket are outside this appearance revision.
assetReviews.notionReview: Re-read the two existing ClothLab ledger rows and matching parent-page bullets. Their generic creative-appearance boundary already covers V4 and contains no quilt colour or patch-count claim, so no Notion or player-facing codex edit was needed. Source verification remains dated 2026-10-24; global repository and unrelated page cursors are preserved.
assetReviews.materialSamplesReview: Muslin, silk, canvas and wool are generic experimental material swatches on identical comparison stands. Their weave, colour, dimensions and simulated response are creative test specifications; no historical issue pattern, wartime object or Tengxian usage is claimed. They introduce no historical assertion requiring an additional player-facing or Notion ledger entry; the existing cloth-study creative boundary remains unchanged.
